$comment: The claims behind docs/acr.md — one entry per WCAG 2.2 success criterion at A and AA. `tools/check-acr.mjs` holds every citation to the repository (a gate's point, a case's title, a sentence in a source, an open finding in the plan) and renders the report; a row cannot say more than a gate proves. Edit this file, run `node tools/check-acr.mjs --write`, never the report.

assistiveTechnology.views: the sandbox views the axe sweep audits (`SBX_ROUTES` in `apps/sandbox-e2e/src/a11y.spec.ts`)

criteria.remarks: The library draws no image that carries meaning on its own. Icons stand inside `<pct-icon>` with `aria-hidden` and take their meaning from the control that holds them; a control's accessible name is written on the tag the consumer types and forwarded to the element that carries the role, so a name is never written where nothing reads it. The words of a name are the consumer's.

titles: the ${path} view has no violations

criteria.remarks: No component renders audio or video: the templates hold no `<audio>` and no `<video>` element, and the gate scans them for one on every run.
No media, so nothing to caption — the same scan as 1.2.1.
No media, so nothing to describe — the same scan as 1.2.1.
No media, live or recorded — the same scan as 1.2.1.
No media — the same scan as 1.2.1.

A label reaches its control through `for` or `aria-labelledby`, a hint and an error through `aria-describedby`, a group through its role and its name — the wiring is the library's and gated, the text is the consumer's. The one relation that was known wrong — an empty `pct-select` panel rendering a `role="listbox"` that owned no `role="option"`, which axe rates critical — was repaired on 2026-09-06: the panel is a surface, the listbox is the list inside it, and the empty panel is a scene of the audit in its own right.

titles: a form in the error state has no violations
an open panel with headings
an empty panel
the wrapper renders the validation error and binds it to the control

criteria.remarks: Reading order is DOM order. No stylesheet names a physical side of the inline axis, so nothing is moved somewhere the DOM does not say, and the right-to-left direction is measured rather than assumed.

titles: the field affix moves to the other side of the control
the select panel inherits the direction from the trigger, not from body

criteria.remarks: The library's own sentences come through `PCT_TEXTS` — every one of them, the gate refuses a literal in a template — and none names a shape, a size, a position or a sound. Instructions around a component are the consumer's.
No stylesheet reads the orientation; the components lay out the same either way. The gate scans every stylesheet for an `orientation` media feature.

The text and date fields are the native `<input>` the consumer writes, so an `autocomplete` purpose written on the tag stays on the element. The number field writes `autocomplete="off"` by default — a browser's formatted string is a value its parser refuses — and takes an `autocomplete` input typed as the platform's own `AutoFill`, so the three numeric purposes on the criterion's list (`bday-day`, `bday-month`, `bday-year`) can be declared on it.

titles: refuses autofill until a consumer asks for it
takes the purpose a consumer declares

criteria.remarks: No state is carried by colour alone: forced colours strip every author colour and the suite reads each state back through position, text or the system palette; an error is a sentence in an alert, not a red edge; the chosen tab, the checked box and the current page each carry an attribute.

titles: the switch carries its state in the thumb’s position, not in a colour

criteria.remarks: Nothing plays sound — the same scan as 1.2.1.

Every colour a stylesheet paints stands as a foreground/background pair in the contrast policy, measured on every token build for both themes at 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for large text; axe measures the composed DOM again, in three engines, every view.

titles: a card with a dark stage has no violations

criteria.remarks: Every component of the library stands on one page (`/all`) with the root font size doubled, and no box that clips is left with content outside it. Text alone is enlarged rather than the page zoomed — zoom scales the layout with the text and would measure nothing.

titles: text at 200 % cuts nothing off

criteria.remarks: The library ships no image of text: icons are glyph drawings without a `<text>` element, and every word is live text. The gate scans the templates and the drawings for one.

All thirty-five sandbox views laid out at 320 CSS pixels, one case each, in three engines: the document may not be scrolled on the inline axis at all. Two harness defects and one library one came out of the first run — a column of flex items sized to their own content, a grid track with a 280 px floor, and a field whose automatic minimum was the native input's twenty-character intrinsic width; `pct-field` now carries `min-width: 0` so it shrinks instead of pushing the page sideways.

titles: lays out at 320 px with nothing to scroll sideways

criteria.remarks: Borders, the focus ring and the states of the controls are `UI` pairs in the same contrast policy as the text, held at 3:1 in both themes on every token build.

The criterion's own four declarations — line height 1.5, letter spacing 0.12 em, word spacing 0.16 em, paragraph spacing 2 em — applied with `!important` over everything on the page that holds every component, with no box that clips left holding content outside it.

titles: own text spacing cuts nothing off

criteria.remarks: The tooltip is the only content that appears on hover or on focus, and each of the criterion's three demands is measured: Escape dismisses it and leaves focus where it was, the pointer can travel onto it, and it stays until the pointer or the focus leaves.

titles: Escape dismisses it and leaves focus where it was (WCAG 1.4.13)
the pointer can travel onto the panel and read it
the leave is waited out rather than cut off

criteria.remarks: Every component's keyboard map is tested key by key in three engines, or its card argues why the map is empty (nothing focusable) or the platform's own (a native button).

titles: the keyboard: the arrows, Home/End, Enter and aria-activedescendant

criteria.remarks: The modal dialog is the one deliberate trap, and Escape leaves it; a menu, a popover, a tooltip, the date panel and the select close on Escape and hand focus back to their trigger.

titles: it takes focus on open and gives it back on close
Escape closes it and says so
Escape closes it and gives focus back to the trigger
Escape closes it and gives focus back to the trigger

criteria.remarks: The only single-character keys are the type-ahead of a list, a menu and a select, active while that component has focus and nowhere else — the exception the criterion names. No `accesskey` is written anywhere; the gate scans for one.

The toast is the only timed content. Each message names its own `duration` (`null` keeps it up), an urgent message waits, and the whole stack pauses while the pointer or the focus rests on it — that rest is how the user extends the time.

titles: an urgent message is an alert, and it waits

criteria.remarks: The brand's gradient no longer runs unattended: every face of `[pctHero]` and the button's `hero` variant run ONE pass of four seconds and then stand still, so the second of the criterion's three conditions is not met for them, and `paused` gives a page a stop of its own besides. Three mechanisms, in this order: `prefers-reduced-motion` is the reader's and outranks both, `paused` is the page's, and the settle is what happens when neither has spoken. What remains is the skeleton's sheen, which travels for as long as the wait does and is meant to: a busy indicator that stopped would say the work had finished. It is `aria-hidden`, so the wait itself is announced by the `aria-busy` region a consumer writes around it, and the movement is that same fact in the sighted channel. Whether that meets the criterion's own “essential” exception is an argument rather than a measurement, so this row says Partially Supports and names both the owner (finding 4.45) and the consumer's part: end the wait, and the motion ends with it.

titles: the sweep runs its pass and stands still inside five seconds
`paused` stops the sweep where it stands
the reduction covers every control, not the button alone
a skeleton’s sheen slows to the loop token and does not stop

criteria.remarks: Nothing flashes. The fastest periodic motion in the library is the spinner's turn and the sheen's loop, both far below three cycles a second, and every duration comes from the motion axis rather than from a stylesheet.

titles: the transitions disappear and a continuous indicator only slows down

criteria.remarks: A page-level criterion: the blocks a page repeats are the consumer's. The library's regions announce themselves — the dialog is a `role="dialog"`, the toast stack a `role="log"`, the breadcrumb and the pager named landmarks.

titles: a named landmark holding a counted list of steps
the pager is a named landmark with a list inside it

criteria.remarks: A page-level criterion; the library sets no document title.

Focus order is DOM order: no positive `tabindex` anywhere (scanned), a dialog takes focus on open and gives it back on close, a menu and a popover return it to their trigger. A toast's action stands at the end of the document because the stack is a child of `body` — reachable, and far; 4.16 in the plan keeps that walk in view.

titles: it takes focus on open and gives it back on close
opening puts focus on the first command
Escape closes it and gives focus back to the trigger
focus goes to the panel, and Tab from there reaches the content

criteria.remarks: The library's own links are the breadcrumb's and the pager's; each carries its visible text or a name from `PCT_TEXTS`, the current one says it is current, and axe's `link-name` runs over every view.

titles: every link is reachable by its exact name — the separator adds nothing
the current page is announced as current, and only one is

criteria.remarks: A page-level criterion about finding pages within a set; the library ships no pages.
A dialog is named by its heading, a field by its label, a group by its legend — wired by the library, worded by the consumer; the gate refuses a name written where nothing reads it.

titles: an open dialog

criteria.remarks: One focus ring, one token, drawn with `:focus-visible` by every control that takes focus (a field draws it around its whole row) and measured as a `UI` pair at 3:1 in both themes; under forced colours it is drawn in `Highlight`.

titles: the focus ring is drawn in Highlight, not in the border colour

evidence.says: The chrome draws focus around the whole row

criteria.remarks: The library keeps one fixed layer on screen — the toast stack, in a corner — and anchors every panel to its trigger. With a standing toast open, every focusable of the view is focused in turn and the element under the middle of its own box is asked for: it is the control itself and not the stack. `elementsFromPoint` and not a rectangle comparison, because a box that overlaps another is not obscured if it is the one in front.

titles: a standing toast leaves every control in front of it

criteria.remarks: No component needs a path or a multipoint gesture: the slider is the native range (a press lands the thumb, the keys move it) and everything else is a press.

titles: a press lands the drawn thumb where the pointer is, and a drag keeps it there
a long press opens it, a tap does not

criteria.remarks: The library's own pointer handling completes on `click` — the field row activates on the up-event, never on `mousedown` — and its triggers are native buttons; the one down-event behaviour is the native range's, whose move the up-event completes.

The visible label is the accessible name: `<label for>` and `aria-labelledby` point at the very text that is shown, so the name contains what is read; an icon-only button is named by the tooltip that shows on it.

titles: every link is reachable by its exact name — the separator adds nothing
an icon-only button is named by its tooltip, open or not

criteria.remarks: Nothing listens to device motion or orientation; the gate scans the sources for a listener.
The slider is the only dragging there is, and a press on the track or the arrow keys do the same without a drag.

titles: a press lands the drawn thumb where the pointer is, and a drag keeps it there

criteria.remarks: A stricter promise than the criterion: 24 × 24 px outright, with no spacing exception, measured per control — the smallest control height is 28 px, and a field's border and affixes are part of its hit area.

titles: a click on the left border padding focuses the field
the field and the button at size ${size} have the same height

criteria.remarks: A page-level criterion; the library sets no `lang` on the document.
The library renders no text in a language of its own: every string it speaks comes through `PCT_TEXTS`, so a passage in another language cannot come from the library.
Focus alone changes nothing: a select opens on a press or a key, never on arriving; a tooltip on focus only describes; the field row's own focus moves nothing.

titles: the keyboard opens it and a click does not
a click opens the panel; picking closes it and shows the label

criteria.remarks: Changing a value submits nothing and navigates nowhere: picking an option closes the panel it came from, a toggle leaves the panel standing, and a form turns valid only when the consumer's schema says so.

titles: a click opens the panel; picking closes it and shows the label
the keyboard toggles the active row and leaves the panel standing
the form turns valid only once every required field is filled

criteria.remarks: A criterion across pages; the library ships no navigation of pages.
A criterion across pages. Within the library one component is one role and one naming rule, held by the gate; the words are the consumer's.
A criterion across pages about where help is found; the library ships no help mechanism.
An error is a sentence: the field's alert region speaks the schema's message, the control says `aria-invalid`, and the message replaces the hint below the field — one line, never two.

titles: the wrapper renders the validation error and binds it to the control
there is one line below the field: the error replaces the hint

criteria.remarks: Every control takes a `label`, a `hint` and a required sign, drawn by the control outside a field and by the field inside one; a control whose widget sits inside its template exposes `ariaLabel` and `ariaLabelledby`, and the gate holds both.

titles: a form in the error state has no violations

criteria.remarks: The text of the first error is the consumer's own message, delivered where the user reads it; the library adds the channel and takes nothing away.

evidence.says: the text of the first error

criteria.remarks: An application-level criterion about legal and financial commitments; the library ships no such flow.
An application-level criterion about information asked twice in one process; the library ships no process.
An application-level criterion; the library ships no authentication.

Every widget is native where the platform has one and an APG pattern where it has not; the name written on the host reaches the element with the role, states are attributes, and axe's ARIA rules run over every view and every special state in three engines. The one value known wrong — the empty select's listbox — was repaired on 2026-09-06; what a screen reader makes of the rest is the pass this report still owes.

titles: the ${path} view has no violations
the a11y gate really does detect violations (a control of the gate)

criteria.remarks: A status is announced from where it happens: the toast stack is a `role="log"` and an urgent message a `role="alert"`, the field's error an alert, the select's empty panel a polite announcement, a refused day is said out loud — each measured. The announcer's assertive channel has no caller yet (4.15 in the plan), so nothing rides it.

titles: an urgent message is an alert, and it waits
opening it announces the text the application translated
a refused day is reached, announced and not takeable
